answers.answer: C) The 30-minute cache TTL exceeds the 15-minute JWT expiry. If user A's data is cached, then user B logs in within the cache window, they may see user A's cached responses. Cache keys should include the user ID or be invalidated on token refresh. This answer correctly connects both pieces of information (JWT expiry and cache TTL) and identifies the root cause: cache duration exceeds authentication token duration, leading to cross-user data leakage. The solution (user-specific cache keys or cache invalidation on auth change) directly addresses the problem.
